primary_work.title: Identifiable Multimodal Causal Representation Learning under Partial Latent Sharing

decision: NARROWED BEYOND PARTIALLY SHARED MULTIMODAL COMPONENT-WISE IDENTIFIABILITY — NOT ADOPTED
excluded_claims: cross-modal language/environment latent alignment is a new identifiability principle
partial latent sharing alone prevents component-wise causal recovery
human-readable modality labels remove component-wise recoding ambiguity
cross-modal transfer or language-shuffle gaps establish target-partition recovery
counterexample: Two models preserve the complete multimodal observable law, shared/specific latent incidence, identifiable causal components, prediction, task, alignment, and language metrics while jointly recoding a fine target partition, raw-utterance classes, denotation map, and language encoder inside an identified shared component.
surviving_rq: After strongest applicable multimodal partial-sharing identification, can a preregistered externally fixed denotation law jointly identify residual target and raw-utterance partitions and trivialize every remaining joint automorphism?
requirements: map SILG channels to modalities and latent subsets
construct equal-observable-law countermodels with different residual partitions
prove language information is unavailable from non-language history
prove residual automorphism group trivial only with anchor
